title: UNEP MARS notification leads an operator to stop a 1,200-tonne methane pipeline leak in Kazakhstan (KAZ_S_136); IMEO observed emissions at the site again by May 2026
summary: UNEP IMEO case KAZ_S_136: pipeline leak first detected Sept 2025, operator rerouted gas, mitigation reported 26 Nov 2025, last emissions 12 Mar 2026; subsequent emissions seen as of 21 May 2026.
account: UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) publishes a Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) case document for source KAZ_S_136. It is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. The document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by DLR's EnMAP on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. Last emissions were detected on 12 March 2026 (document updated 15 April 2026). A footnote states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments and companies. The Chemical Engineer (5 May 2026), relaying UNEP's snapshot, counts one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed Kazakhstan gas-pipeline mitigation of an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither gives a case ID, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established.
purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that operators and governments mitigate them. This case was that purpose.
system: UNEP IMEO Methane Alert and Response System (MARS): satellite plume detection and analysis with AI models, notification and satellite confirmation
deployer: UNEP International Methane Emissions Observatory (notification); unnamed pipeline operator in Kazakhstan (mitigation)
location: Kazakhstan, 43.39767°, 52.49505° (no place name in the UNEP document)
domain: Climate change mitigation / methane emissions monitoring
segment: Oil and gas transmission; intergovernmental observatory

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary is identified. The benefit is an avoided greenhouse-gas release.

The operator stopped a leak of an estimated 1,200 tonnes of methane by rerouting gas after the notification, a material correction to its operations. The operator is unnamed and the leak was later observed again.
One source among thousands of MARS alerts (the trade press counts over 3,500 alerts and about 43 confirmed cases since 2023). Climate benefit limited by the subsequent emissions observed in May 2026.

ai_role.statement: UNEP's case document records detection, notification, the operator's rerouting of gas and satellite confirmation. It names DLR's EnMAP for the plume image. The only description of an AI role is UNEP's general statement that IMEO analyzes satellite data with advanced AI models. The AI contribution to this specific detection is therefore not isolated. The sources are UNEP's own (system operator) plus trade press relaying UNEP. No operator or government statement is among the sources.
